LESSON: NUTRITION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: BIOLOGY
Strand: Anatomy and Physiology of Plants
Topic 2.1: Nutrition
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Nutrition, part of Anatomy and Physiology of Plants in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 BIOLOGY.

Key inquiry question: How do plants obtain food?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Nutrition together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-Efficacy: The learner performs assigned tasks while using illustrations to show reactions of the light and dark

stages of photosynthesis.

● Digital literacy: The learner acquires technological competency as they search for information and watch animations

on the process of photosynthesis.

23

● Communication and Collaboration: The learners develop speaking and listening skills in discussing reactions

involving light and dark stages of photosynthesis.

Values

A learner demonstrates honesty skill as they watch video clips on the process of photosynthesis and discuss with peers by

not deviating to other internet sites.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Unity: The learner cooperates with peers during the searching of information and group discussions on the process of

photosynthesis.

● Respect: The learner displays patience while listening to peers during the discussion on the structure of chloroplast in

relation to its function.

● Integrity: Environmental Conservation: The learner appreciates the need to conserve the environment while watching

animations/video clips on the process of photosynthesis.

● Safety and Security: The learner responsibly uses the internet while searching for information on different types of

nutrition in plants.

Suggested Learning Resources

● Digital devices with assistive technology such as screen readers, talkback, refreshable braille display, screen

magnifiers

● Braille reference materials and Textbooks

● Reference materials in print with appropriate font size and colour contrast

● Tactile diagrams of chloroplasts

Key Skills:

Ability to describe the light and dark stages of photosynthesis
